So we can use cp to copy FinalReport.txt to Archives directory with new name. But cp signature: source, destination. Destination can be a directory or file name. If destination is a directory, source will be copied into this directory. No file paths allowed. So to copy to Archives with new name, we need to specify destination as "ArchivedFinalReport2024.txt"? But that would copy into current directory? Wait: cp source: "FinalReport.txt", destination: "ArchivedFinalReport2024.txt". That will copy into current directory with that name. But we want to copy into Archives directory. Since no paths allowed, we cannot specify path. But maybe we can first cd into Archives then cp. But that would copy into Archives with same name. But we want new name. We can cd into Archives then cp FinalReport.txt ArchivedFinalReport2024.txt. That will copy into Archives with new name. That works. So steps: cd Archives, cp FinalReport.txt ArchivedFinalReport2024.txt. Then maybe cd back. Let\'s do that.')
